name: read
description: Read an /absolute path (on the default machine) or machineId:/absolute/path. UTF-8 text by default with an optional line window (offset, limit); base64 preserves binary bytes.

name: write
description: Create or overwrite one /absolute (default machine) or machineId:/absolute/path file. Parent directories must exist.

name: edit
description: Apply one or more exact literal UTF-8 replacements to one /absolute (default machine) or machineId:/absolute/path file. Each oldText must match exactly once in the original and edits must not overlap. Read/write composition is not atomic against external writers.

name: ls
description: List immediate directory entries at an /absolute path (on the default machine) or machineId:/absolute/path, without following symlinks. limit caps the entries returned.

name: find
description: Find files and directories whose path relative to the search root matches a glob (e.g. **/*.ts). path is /absolute (searched on the default machine) or machineId:/absolute/path. Symlinks are not followed.

name: grep
description: Search UTF-8 file content with a regular expression (literal=true for plain text) at an /absolute path (searched on the default machine) or machineId:/absolute/path. Directories recurse in name order without following symlinks; glob filters file names; context adds surrounding lines; binary files refuse.

name: bash
description: Run a shell command on a machine daemon: the named machine, or the configured default when machine is omitted. cwd must be an absolute path inside an offered export (default /). Execution time is bounded by the daemon. No persistent cwd state. With machine+session, the command is typed into a named persistent terminal (survives daemon restarts; same session name reattaches) and stdout carries terminal output since the previous call; an empty command just reads.

command.description: Shell command. With session it is typed into the terminal; empty reads pending session output.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory inside an offered export; defaults to /.

session.description: Named persistent terminal on the machine. Survives between calls and daemon restarts; same name reattaches.

name: eval
description: Run Python in this session's persistent cell: state survives between calls; machine handles, parallel, completion, browser(machineId) for Chromium automation over CDP, and tool.<name>() proxies are in scope. operation.op=run starts code and waits up to timeout seconds; peek reads a running cell's output so far; stop interrupts it. stop and the 10 minute ceiling discard the interpreter's state.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the cell. A cell still running is answered as running with its cell_id and keeps going in the background.

cell_id.description: The cell_id a run answered with while still running.
The cell_id a run answered with while still running.

name: send_message
description: Send one letter — markdown, code, images, files — or one emoji reaction to a contact: a session, a new child session, a person on a channel (contact id, with surface and conversation to answer where they wrote), a declared CLI agent on an attached machine (cli:<id> — the letter is typed into its terminal; the reply is a prompt pointing at the child's admitted rows), a declared webhook target (webhook:<id> — the letter is POSTed to its URL, signed; the target's textual answer is returned on the result as `response`), or a declared A2A peer (a2a:<id> — the letter goes to the agent as message/send; its answer, or where its task stands, is returned on the result, with `thread` for reply_to to continue the exchange). Otherwise returns a handle without waiting for a reply; the reply arrives as a delivered prompt in this session. A letter to a person on a channel for whom the Owner declared no social budget waits for the Owner's consent. A call requires Owner approval, opens a huddle in to.conversation.channelId from the selected voice surface's account, and talks to the contact live; do not set to.as for calls.

surface.description: Channel to reach the contact on (telegram, slack, …) when they are reachable on several; omit when they have one.

conversation.description: Where on that channel to answer: the chat and thread the contact wrote in (needs surface). Omit to reach them directly.

as.description: Which account the letter goes out under: bot (default) or owner — the Owner's own account, only when the Owner asked you to send from it in this conversation and their account is connected for sending.

message.description: Plain markdown, or a structured message spec — see the Structured messages section of your instructions.

react.description: Instead of a letter, put this emoji on the message the contact wrote (to.conversation.replyToMessageId names it). Channel contacts only.

kind.description: prompt is the default letter; interrupt and resume steer a running session.

reply_to.description: The message this answers; for a webhook or a2a contact, the thread a previous result named, to continue that exchange.

deadline_ms.description: Milliseconds from now after which no reply counts as unknown.

spend_cap.description: Spending cap granted to a new child session; creation without one is refused by policy.

name: provision
description: Administer contacts, channels, credentials, automations, machines, and provisioning status. Use op=contact_add|contact_remove|contact_promote|contact_merge|channel_add|channel_enable|channel_disable|secret_rotate|bundle_enable|bundle_disable|automation_add|automation_remove|automation_enable|automation_disable|automation_list|machine_add|machine_grant|machine_deny|machine_remove|machine_list|status. Authority changes, machine public keys, Owner-account channel instances, their outbound grant and a channel's declared default tier require Owner consent. A contact with reach: true is one the Resident may write to cold. Session-created automations remain disabled until the Owner enables them.

trustTier.description: Standing trust tier for every bound endpoint.

endpoints.description: Platform identities this Person speaks through. externalId by channel: slack TEAM:USER (workspace TEAM), discord the user id, telegram the user id, instagram the user pk, kakaotalk the user id, github the login, linear the user id (workspace the organization id), ws the ?actor= name. A workspace-less endpoint matches in every workspace of the platform.

reach.description: true lets the Resident write to this Person cold through send_message; absent, the Person is an inbound identity only.

timeoutMs.description: Answer window for a guard-opened approval request (default 24h).

identity.description: Which account this instance speaks as: the bot or the Owner's own account. A re-declaration keeps the stored identity; a fresh one is the bot.

outbound.description: Owner instances only: whether the Resident may send from the Owner's account on explicit instruction.

grant.description: Who this surface admits — the Owner's decision, so any grant block takes Owner consent: defaultTier is the tier every sender on it gets who is not a declared Person (absent, only Persons at manager or above are admitted); allowedSenders admits those platform ids alone; mentionOnly routes channel messages only when they address the Resident. A block replaces the stored one (a field left out is cleared); a declaration without a block keeps it.

settings.description: Non-secret knobs; an Owner instance's intake posture. A re-declaration keeps the stored settings.

credential.description: Plaintext credential payload; sealed into the vault, never stored bare.

name.description: The declared bundle name, e.g. monitor.
The declared bundle name, e.g. monitor.

name: completion
description: Ask a sub-model one one-shot, stateless question and return its text. Options: model (an id on the configured provider), system, schema (a JSON Schema the answer must satisfy; the validated JSON text is returned).

prompt.description: One complete instruction for a stateless sub-model call.

model.description: A model id on the configured provider; the default model when omitted.

system.description: System text for the sub-model call.

schema.description: A JSON Schema the answer must satisfy; the validated JSON text is returned.

name: monitor
description: Watch command output in a PTY, a machine terminal session, an absolute path, or a cron schedule outside the session. Create a persistent or timed watch or a recurring cron chain, rearm a retired one, or cancel it.
